narrative:
## Weekly Political Search Interest Briefing: 27 September to 3 October 2026

One Nation had the highest average Google Trends search-interest score among the four tracked parties this week, at 18.0, followed by the Greens at 6.9, Labor at 3.3 and Liberal at 2.4. These are relative interest scores, not search counts, voter support or measures of unique users. The ranking describes weekly averages, not every day: the Greens narrowly exceeded One Nation on 30 September, 18 to 17.

The Greens recorded the reporting week's detected spike on 30 September, with a score of 18, approximately 6.3 times the spike detector's baseline average. Their daily scores ranged from 1 to 18. One Nation ranged from 13 to 27, reaching its weekly peak on 3 October. Labor ranged from 2 to 4 and Liberal from 2 to 3. The other detected spikes occurred in August and are historical context, not events from this reporting week.

The available sentiment analysis was neutral for Labor (+0.00) and One Nation (+0.07), and positive for Liberal (+0.19) and the Greens (+0.21). Labor had 1 positive, 33 neutral and 1 negative classified mentions; Liberal had 6 positive, 19 neutral and 1 negative; the Greens had 6 positive, 23 neutral and no negative; One Nation had 2 positive, 11 neutral and 1 negative. These classifications describe the analysed material, not representative public opinion.

No news data was available for this briefing. The data therefore cannot establish what caused the Greens spike or connect search changes to specific announcements, debates or media coverage. The useful next check is whether that rise persists in subsequent observations, with fresh news evidence needed before attributing a cause.
